title: Book 8 — Urania, Chapter 99
paragraphs: The first message, then, to come to Susa — announcing that Xerxes had Athens in his possession — so greatly delighted the Persians who had been left behind that they strewed all the roads with myrtle boughs and burned incense continually, and kept up sacrifices and feasting themselves. But the second message that arrived afterwards so disturbed them that they all tore their garments and gave themselves over to crying and lamentation without restraint, laying the blame on Mardonius. This the Persians did not so much because they were grieved about the ships as because they feared for Xerxes himself.
